facts.text: The grey butcherbird sings a loud, rollicking territorial song, often performed as a duet or by the whole group.
facts.quote: All members of the territorial group contribute to the territorial song, a loud and rollicking song with both musical and harsh elements.

facts.text: The grey butcherbird preys on small vertebrates, including other small birds, their nestlings and lizards.
facts.quote: The grey butcherbird preys on small vertebrates including other birds.

facts.text: Grey butcherbirds catch more food than they need and store the surplus in the fork of a branch to eat later.
facts.quote: They have a tendency to catch more food than they need and have a habit to store food in the fork of a branch to be consumed later.

facts.text: It hunts by sitting and waiting, then pouncing on prey on the ground or striking small birds and insects in flight.
facts.quote: Prey is captured by the grey butcherbird sally-pouncing the prey on the ground. Small birds and insects can be captured in flight by using sally-striking.

facts.text: The grey butcherbird has adapted well to city living and can be found in the suburbs of many Australian cities.
facts.quote: It appears to be adapting well to city living, and can be encountered in the suburbs of many Australian cities including Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney and Hobart.

facts.text: The adult has a black head, a white chin and throat, and a beak with a slight downwards hook at the tip.
facts.quote: The adult grey butcherbird has a black head, top and sides; and a white chin and throat through to the lower hindneck.

facts.text: Grey butcherbirds usually breed in single territorial pairs from July to January, and both sexes defend the territory all year.
facts.quote: The grey butcherbird usually breed in single territorial pairs from July to January. Both sexes defend their territories and nest throughout the year.

facts.text: The nest is a shallow bowl of sticks and twigs, lined with grasses and usually built within 10 m of the ground.
facts.quote: The nest is a shallow, bowl-shaped made from sticks and twigs. The nest is lined with grasses and other soft fibres. Nests are normally located within 10 m (33 ft) off the ground.
